title: What does XChainCreateBridge do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XChainCreateBridge and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, XChainCreateBridge defines a bridge between designated door accounts on two chains. [1]

The configuration identifies both chains' assets and the relevant door accounts and reward parameters. Compatible configuration and witness arrangements are needed for transfers to work. A bridge definition is not a universal interoperability guarantee. Inspect the trust assumptions and both networks before treating an asset on one side as automatically equivalent to an asset on the other. [1]

The XChainCreateBridge reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using XChainCreateBridge, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
